column1:
Policy and institutional 
framework creates a favorable 
environment for state and non-
state stakeholders to address 
gender equity in skills, vocational, 
and tertiary education.
column2:
• 	What	are	the	policy	gaps	in	relation	
to women’s needs and interests?
• 	How	to	make	policy	more	
transformative for women? 
• 	Are	there	policy	provisions	
regarding gender mainstreaming in 
education and skills that can be used 
to justify action proposed?
column3:
• 	National	dialogue	for	aligning	
internationally acknowledged gender 
dimensions with national policies and 
strategies needed
• 	Identification	of	present	policy	provisions	
that promote greater involvement of 
women and girls in skills, vocational, and 
tertiary education
• 	Developing	policy	monitoring	and	
accountability mechanisms that would 
include women and girls as stakeholders

column1:
Existing policies and provisions 
for women’s entrepreneurship 
should be aligned with education 
and skills development policies 
so that the area of skills for 
entrepreneurship is supported.
column2:
• 	What	are	the	areas	of	skill	gaps	for	
women’s entrepreneurship in both 
urban and rural areas?
• 	What	are	the	skill	gaps	for	different	
age groups and sectors?
• 	Where	and	how	are	skills	training	
provided? Is it appropriate for 
women entrepreneurs?
column3:
• 	Market	research	on	demand	for	
training by women entrepreneurs and 
identification of areas of unserved needs
• 	Scoping	of	training	available	for	women	
entrepreneurs and identification of gaps
• 	Identification	of	private	sector,	
nongovernment organization, and 
government providers of training and on-
the-job support for women entrepreneurs

column1:
Secondary, tertiary, and vocational 
education are more responsive 
to market needs and gender 
considerations.
column2:
• 	Where	are	women	situated	in	the	
labor market currently?
• 	Where	are	potential	areas	for	
women to enter?
• 	Are	there	good	examples	of	
nontraditional and potential 
occupations for women that can be 
adopted from the region?
• 	What	are	the	constraints	for	women	
to enter and stay in better-paid and 
more productive occupations?
column3:
• 	Developing	partnerships	with	employers’	
associations and trade unions 
• 	Carrying	out	market	surveys	of	demand	
for labor
• 	Media	campaigns	to	challenge	stereotypes	
on occupational segregation
• 	Skills	development	to	be	supplemented	by	
job placements and job counseling
